title: Speier et al. 2017 — A comparison of stimulus types in online classification of the P300 speller using language models
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 10 healthy participants performing a P300 speller task using a 6×6 character matrix. The study compares two stimulus conditions—famous faces and inverted faces—to evaluate their effects on online P300 classification performance using language models. Data were collected across 2 sessions per subject with 3 runs per session, sampled at 256 Hz from 32 EEG channels.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a g.tec amplifier at 256 Hz sampling rate from 32 channels arranged in a standard 1005 montage, with left ear reference and AFz ground. Participants performed an online P300 row-column speller task with a 6×6 character matrix under two stimulus conditions (famous faces and inverted faces). Visual feedback was provided. Inter-stimulus interval was 25 ms with stimulus onset asynchrony of 125 ms. Trial duration was 1.0 s with approximately 1200 flashes per training run.
